personalSubscriptions.heading: Personal subscriptions (individual use only)
personalSubscriptions.intro: Claude (Pro/Max), GLM (Z.ai Coding Plan) and ChatGPT (Codex) are each licensed to you as an individual, so they are stored just for you and only your runs use them. Each token is encrypted under a personal password (never stored) that you enter when you start such a run; it is cached in this browser for a while so it stays out of your way. The password is a low-friction convenience and a transparency signal that the system will not silently share your credential, not a wall against a system-key holder. These models cannot be used on recurring schedules.

composeEnvSetup.title: Guided Docker Compose setup for a service
composeEnvSetup.lead: Walks one service through building the Docker Compose recipe its test environments are stood up from, instead of hand-writing the compose path and setup steps.

how.title: How it works
how.scan: Scans the service's linked repository for compose files, profiles, env files and seed dumps.
how.analyse: Optionally runs the environment analyst agent to draft setup steps and a health gate from the repository's own scripts.
how.preflight: Runs the recipe's preflight checks on the machine that will provision it.
how.save: Saves the recipe onto the service and registers the workspace's Docker Compose handler.
how.outcome: After that the Deployer stands up exactly that stack whenever a pipeline needs a live environment, and the Tester runs against it. Nothing is applied until you save.

needed.title: You need this when
needed.running: The service's tests need the app actually running: API or UI tests, migrations, seeded data.
needed.compose: The service is provisioned as Docker Compose and has no recipe saved yet.
needed.setup: Standing the stack up takes more than one command: profiles, env files, seed data or a readiness check.

notNeeded.title: You can skip it when

runTask.description: Open a task, choose its pipeline and start the agents working.

intro.title: From task to run
intro.body: A task on the board is a request. Opening it shows the pipeline that will deliver it and the controls that start it.

openTask.title: Open a task
openTask.body: Clicking a card opens its inspector, which is where everything about that task lives.

inspector.title: The inspector
inspector.body: Status, repository, pipeline and the run itself: this panel is the task's whole story.

pipeline.title: Choose a pipeline
pipeline.body: A pipeline is the sequence of agents that will do the work: write a spec, build it, review it, run the checks, merge it. Pick the one that fits the task.

start.title: Starting a run
start.body: This starts the pipeline for real, and agents spend model budget. So the click is yours to make: press it whenever you are ready, during this tour or after it.

steps.title: Watching it work
steps.body: Every step reports its own progress here as it runs, pushed live. Click a step to read what the agent actually produced.

finish.title: That is the loop
finish.body: Plan a task, pick a pipeline, start it, watch it. The walkthroughs after this one read a real run, so they unlock once you have actually started one.

answerPark.title: Answer a waiting run
answerPark.description: A run has paused for a human. See where it asks, and how to reply.

intro.title: A run is waiting for you
intro.body: Some steps stop and ask: a question about the requirements, a plan to approve, a choice between approaches. A paused run waits for an answer indefinitely, so nothing moves until you reply.

resolve.title: Where it asks
resolve.body: A task waiting on a human says so on its card and offers this action. It takes you straight to whatever is being asked.

decide.title: Choosing an answer
decide.body: Each option is a real instruction to the run: pick one and the pipeline carries on from there with your choice.

approve.title: Approving the work
approve.body: Approve to let the run continue, or request changes to send the step back with your notes. Both are answers, and the run resumes either way.

finish.title: Nothing waits silently
finish.body: Waiting tasks are marked on the board and counted in the toolbar, so you can find them without hunting.

reviewMerge.title: Review and merge
reviewMerge.description: Read what a finished run produced, and get it merged.

intro.title: A run finished
intro.body: Finished is not the same as shipped. A task is done when its pull request is merged, so this tour is the last mile.

openTask.title: Open the task
openTask.body: Open a task whose run has finished. Its inspector holds the full step list.

openStep.title: Open a step
openStep.body: Clicking a step opens what that agent produced: its report, its findings and what it changed.

result.title: Reading the result
result.body: This is the agent's own account of the work. Review steps list findings, a tester reports verdicts, the merger explains how it scored the change.

merge.title: Merging
merge.body: When a run opens a pull request, the inspector offers the merge here. A pipeline with a merger step can also merge for itself when the change scores above your threshold.

finish.title: Shipped
finish.body: Merged work marks the task done on the board. That is the whole loop: plan, run, answer, review, merge.

wireModels.title: Connect a model provider
wireModels.description: Point the workspace at the engines your agents run on.

intro.title: Agents need an engine
intro.body: Every step of every pipeline is a model call, so nothing runs until this workspace can reach a provider. This tour shows where that connection lives.

open.title: Model providers
open.body: This opens the providers hub: every engine this deployment can connect, with the ones already wired marked as connected.

hub.title: Pick how you connect
hub.body: One gateway key unlocks a wide catalogue at once. A vendor key, a personal plan or a model runner on your own machine work just as well, and you can hold several at the same time.

finish.title: Then choose per agent
finish.body: Model configuration, in the same sidebar section, sets which model each agent kind uses. Cheap steps can run on cheap models and the hard ones on your best, without editing a single pipeline.

designPipeline.title: Design a pipeline
designPipeline.description: Assemble the agents that deliver a task, and save it for any task to run.

intro.title: The sequence is yours
intro.body: A pipeline is the ordered set of agents that turns a task into a merged pull request. The built-in ones cover most work, and this tour opens the builder where you can shape your own.

open.title: Build a pipeline
open.body: The builder opens beside the board, so the work stays in view while you shape the flow.

palette.title: The agent palette
palette.body: Every agent kind this deployment ships is listed here, from the ones that plan the work to the ones that review, test and merge it. Click one to append it as a step.

chain.title: The chain you are building
chain.body: Steps run top to bottom, and each row carries its own switches: attach the reviewer that sends a step back when it scores too low, require your approval before the next one starts, or run a step as a panel of several models.

save.title: Saving your pipeline
save.body: Save becomes available once the draft holds at least one step. A saved pipeline joins the library in this window and is offered wherever a task picks one; name it for the job it does rather than the agents in it, because that name is all you see when choosing later.

finish.title: Ready to run
finish.body: Cloning a built-in is the quickest start: copy the closest one, change a step, save it under your own name. Nothing you save takes effect until a task is actually started with it.

agentStandards.title: Set the standards agents follow
agentStandards.description: Curate the guidelines every agent reads before it touches your code.

intro.title: Standards, not instructions
intro.body: Context fragments are the house rules: conventions, review criteria and best practices folded into an agent's prompt on every run. Curating them is how you steer the output instead of restating the same rules in every task.

open.title: Context fragments
open.body: This opens the library for this board.

library.title: One merged catalog
library.body: The built-in catalog, your account's fragments and this board's own are merged into a single list, with the closer tier winning. You can write one here, import a document, or link a repository folder so files you already maintain stay the source of truth.

finish.title: Where they land
finish.body: A service or a task can narrow which fragments its agents get, and the board-wide defaults live in Workspace settings. Agents that write code are given a condensed brief of each fragment, so a long standard never crowds out the task itself.

connectSystems.title: Connect the systems you already use
connectSystems.description: Trackers, documents, chat and monitors, and what each one adds to a run.

intro.title: Runs can reach further
intro.body: Issues can arrive from your tracker, requirements from your documents, notifications in your team chat, and release health from your monitors. Every connection is optional, and each one changes what a run can see or say.

open.title: The integrations hub
open.body: One list of every external system this workspace can link, with whatever is connected already marked.

hub.title: Connect what you need
hub.body: Source control comes first, because pipelines need code to work on. The rest can wait until the question comes up: a tracker to pull issues from, a document source for requirements context, chat for notifications, monitors to watch a release after it ships.

finish.title: Yours or the workspace's
finish.body: Some entries belong to you rather than to the board, such as a personal access token or plan, and are used only for runs you start. The hub marks which is which, and My setup collects the ones that are yours.

diagnoseFailure.title: Read a failure
diagnoseFailure.description: A run stopped with an error. Find out what broke, and what to do about it.

intro.title: Runs fail, and that is normal
intro.body: A failed run is not a dead end. The board keeps the error, the cause is usually one line, and most causes are fixed by a setting rather than by rewriting the task.

banner.title: What went wrong
banner.body: The card swaps its progress bar for this banner. It names the cause, the details hold the raw output, and some causes offer a button straight to the setting that fixes them.

retry.title: Run it again
retry.body: Retry re-runs the work. Earlier errors stay on the task under Previous errors, so you can compare attempts instead of losing the trail.

finish.title: A failure is information
finish.body: Fix the cause, retry, compare. If the same error keeps coming back, the details are what to bring to whoever can widen a permission or connect what is missing.

prepareInfrastructure.title: Where runs happen
prepareInfrastructure.description: The machines agents run on, the environments they test in, and the credentials they may use.

intro.title: Agents need somewhere to run
intro.body: Every container step runs on an execution backend, tests come up in an environment, and some capabilities need a credential. All three are configured in one window.

open.title: Open Infrastructure
open.body: Everything about where and how runs execute lives here.

tabs.title: One tab per concern
tabs.body: Agent containers is where runs execute. Test environments is what a service is brought up from. The credential list shows which keys the capabilities your agents use can actually resolve, and which are still missing.

finish.title: Failures point back here
finish.body: When a run fails while provisioning, this is the window its banner is asking you to open. Worth knowing before that happens rather than after.

panelReviews.title: Review by panel
panelReviews.description: Have several models review the same work instead of one, on the tasks that warrant it.

intro.title: One reviewer, or several
intro.body: A review step normally runs one agent. It can instead run a panel of several models and compare what they say, which catches what a single reviewer misses on heavier work.

open.title: Open Model configuration
open.body: Panels are made of models, so they are set up beside them.

groups.title: Define a panel
groups.body: A group names the models on the panel and how demanding a task has to be before it is used. A step then selects a group instead of naming models one by one.

finish.title: Cost follows effort
finish.body: A panel costs as many model calls as it has members, which is why a group can be limited to the tasks whose estimate clears its bar. Small work keeps a single reviewer.

shareServices.title: The services you already run
shareServices.description: Tell the agents which shared systems exist, and what their APIs look like.

intro.title: Do not rebuild what you have
intro.body: Agents design in the dark unless they know what your organisation already runs. This catalog names those systems and carries their API contracts.

open.title: Open Foundational services
open.body: The catalog of shared capabilities available to every board in this workspace.

catalog.title: Register, upload, or sync
catalog.body: Add a service by hand, upload its API documents, or link a repository and let them sync. Designs then reference what is registered here instead of inventing an interface.

finish.title: Design steps read this
finish.body: A design that declares which of these it uses gets their full contracts in the next step. One that declares nothing gets nothing, so keeping this current is what makes it work.

unavailable.title: Can't open {tool}
unavailable.missingMetadata: Fill in {fields} on the Metadata tab of Workspace settings first.
unavailable.unresolved: This tool did not return an address for the current workspace.
unavailable.resolverFailed: This tool failed while working out its address. The cause is in the browser console, for whoever maintains this deployment.
unavailable.unsafeUrl: This tool returned an address that is not a web link, so it was not opened.
